results.title: coverforest: Conformal Predictions with Random Forest in Python - ADS
results.content: ## coverforest: Conformal Predictions with Random Forest in Python. Conformal prediction provides a framework for uncertainty quantification, specifically in the forms of prediction intervals and sets with distribution-free guaranteed coverage. While recent cross-conformal techniques such as CV+ and Jackknife+-after-bootstrap achieve better data efficiency than traditional split conformal methods, they incur substantial computational costs due to required pairwise comparisons between training and test samples' out-of-bag scores. Observing that these methods naturally extend from ensemble models, particularly random forests, we leverage existing optimized random forest implementations to enable efficient cross-conformal predictions. We present coverforest, a Python package that implements efficient conformal prediction methods specifically optimized for random forests. coverforest supports both regression and classification tasks through various conformal prediction methods, including split conformal, CV+, Jackknife+-after-bootstrap, and adaptive prediction sets. Our experiments demonstrate that coverforest's predictions achieve the desired level of coverage. The source code for the coverforest is hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/donlap/coverforest. Code available at https://github.com/donlap/coverforest.

results.title: Mastering stock predictions with Random Forest
results.content: # Mastering stock predictions with Random Forest | by Avetik Babayan | Python in Plain English. ## Python in Plain English. Image 2: Python in Plain English. # Mastering stock predictions with Random Forest. Ladies and Gentlemen, please give a warm welcome to our hero-of-the-day, the RandomForest methodology! ### What is a Random Forest? It builds upon the simplicity of decision trees by creating an “ensemble” or a “forest” of trees instead of relying on a single decision tree. The Random Forest algorithm works by creating multiple decision trees during the training phase. Each tree in the forest is built from a random sample of the training set, and at each node in the tree, a subset of features is randomly selected to determine the split. For regression tasks, the final prediction is usually the average of the predictions from all the trees in the forest. ## Published in Python in Plain English.
